Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott

Class OttLinkAuthenticationProvider

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott.OttLinkAuthenticationProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationProvider
public class OttLinkAuthenticationProvider extends Object implements org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationProvider
Confirms a magic link: consumes the token Spring's JdbcOneTimeTokenService stored and signs the user in with it. It does what Spring's own provider does, except that it also reads the purpose the link was requested for (LinkTokenUsername), which Spring's provider cannot because it would look the marked user name up as it is:
  • a link requested for a sign-in answers with the user's authentication plus FACTOR_OTT;
  • a link requested as a second factor is refused unless the session that confirms it is the signed-in session of the same user, with a primary factor, and OttSecondFactorChannels allows the e-mail channel for that session (it did not sign the user in, and the user has no other confirmed second factor); it then answers with the second-factor authority of the e-mail channel, and Spring Security's authentication filter merges it with the factors the session holds.
Links are delivered by e-mail only. The account is loaded through the user service of the chain, which refuses a disabled, locked or expired account.
